title: Understanding the DataFrame
text: The DataFrame $$'song_{sample'}$$ contains columns for song title, artist, genre, and streams. The 'streams' column is the target variable, and 'genre' is used to create features.

title: Feature Engineering Process
text: The code creates binary features for each unique genre by checking if the genre matches the current genre in the loop. This results in a one-hot encoding of the 'genre' column.

title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding creates a new column for each unique category in the 'genre' column, with a $$1$$ if the row belongs to that category and $$0$$ otherwise.

title: Linear Regression with One-Hot Encoding
text: When using one-hot encoding, if all categories are included, the matrix $$X^T$$ X becomes singular (not invertible) because of perfect multicollinearity.

hintAnswer: Because all categories are included in the $$one-hot$$ encoding, leading to perfect multicollinearity.
